author: Matt Larkin
title: Matt Larkin’s fantasy hockey top 300 player rankings for 2026-27

players.writeup_summary: Elite, durable multi-category superstar with huge shot volume; a legitimate first-overall option.
Safest elite point producer available, though his goal and shot totals fluctuate more than MacKinnon’s.
Already an elite scorer at 20 with first-overall upside, tempered only by possible sophomore-style regression.
Still belongs in the first-overall conversation, with age being the main reason for slight caution.
Per-game production remains elite, but recent missed games and load management add durability risk.
Exceptionally dependable 100-point winger with elite durability and strong odds of returning above 40 goals.
Still Larkin’s top fantasy defenseman, though today’s deep crop of elite offensive blueliners narrows his positional advantage.
Bankable first-round winger who produces near a 100-point pace despite lacking an elite center.
Offers Makar-level offensive upside with extraordinary durability; last season’s 95 points may represent his peak.
Excellent fit beside Colorado’s stars; some goal regression is possible but 90-plus points remains realistic.
Team-driving defenseman with rare goal and shot production and even more upside if moved to a contender.
Still in his prime and producing at an elite rate since joining Dallas; little reason for concern.
Larkin’s safest goalie choice thanks to sustained elite rate stats, workload and league-leading win potential.
Extremely high scoring floor with possible contract-year upside; an ideal low-risk early selection.
Already matched elite defenseman production in Year 2 and could eventually push beyond 90 points.
Elite point-producing defenseman and a safe roster cornerstone despite a lower goal ceiling than some peers.
Coming off a 100-point Selke season with enough surrounding talent to sustain a very high scoring floor.
One of fantasy’s safest goal scorers, routinely delivering roughly 40-plus goals and around 90 points.
Established 50-goal upside with another 45-plus season plausible, though last year may represent his points ceiling.
Young star whose underlying scoring profile suggests last year’s 86 points could be closer to his floor than ceiling.
Elite shot generator whose 41-goal breakout looks sustainable, with potential to challenge for league shot and goal leads.
Florida’s deeper supporting cast could lift his points while his huge shot and hit totals remain intact.
Still appears to have another offensive gear and could push toward 90 points in his prime.
No longer the peripheral-stat monster he once was, but remains a point-per-game defenseman contributing across categories.
Extremely reliable high-end goal scorer; a modest overall point ceiling keeps him just outside Round 1.
Consistent 90-point center with 100-point upside if he finally puts together a full healthy season.
Five straight seasons of strong goal and point totals give him a higher floor than many comparable stars.
Health lowers his expected value, but even a reduced season can produce strong goal totals and monster upside remains.
Larkin expects a rebound toward roughly 90 points after an adjustment year in Vegas.
Elite when active, but three straight seasons around 60 games make first-round pricing difficult to justify.
Top-tier production when healthy, but substantial annual injury risk demands a discount.
Already a record-setting young goal-scoring defenseman; 70 points is plausible even without an improved supporting cast.
Has emerged as a true Washington workhorse after two excellent seasons and could finish as fantasy’s top goalie.
Suspension and trade uncertainty create enormous draft risk despite his established elite-goalie ceiling.
Young two-way star offers a point-per-game floor and 100-point upside, though Anaheim’s winger situation creates uncertainty.
Reliable 80-plus-point producer who also contributes hits and may still have another level at age 24.
One of hockey’s most dependable 30-goal, 80-point wingers; age slightly limits the upside premium.
Elite rate-stat goalie whose weaker Islanders team primarily limits his win ceiling.
Coming off a career-best 103 points; regression is possible, but elite shooting efficiency supports strong goal totals.
Prime-age winger attached to an elite offense with a dependable scoring floor and continued goal upside.
Consistent 35-goal scorer whose chemistry with Panarin creates legitimate career-year potential.
High-floor starter on a strong Dallas team who still has room for a true Vezina-level fantasy season.
Strong enough individually to remain valuable despite team weakness; wins are the main limitation.
Age has ended the 100-point ceiling, but he remains a high-end 30-goal, 80-point type contributor.
Extremely safe point-per-game winger, though Cooley’s rise may gradually reduce his team-leading playmaking role.
One of fantasy’s best category-fillers among defensemen thanks to points, shots, hits and blocks.
Consistent high-end offensive defenseman whose current market price may undersell his long-term 70-point production.
Rapidly ascending young scorer with 45-to-50-goal upside on an improving Utah roster.
Strong bounce-back candidate with a long history of 30-plus goals and an improved Florida environment.
Proven 40-goal scorer, but Detroit’s roster turmoil makes his linemates and near-term ceiling unusually uncertain.
Extremely dependable center who should provide 25-plus goals, 75-plus points and strong durability.
Still productive entering age 39, but increasing injury risk needs to be incorporated into his price.
Excellent individual goalie, though Boston’s defensive environment may make last season’s results difficult to repeat.
Still improving as Anaheim’s surrounding talent develops; a 70-point defense season is within reach.
Dynamic rising star who could become Utah’s leading scorer, with injury history the main caution.
Veteran winger remains a reliable source of goals, shots, points and hits even after his peak.
Bankable 70-plus-point winger whose ceiling may be constrained by Detroit’s stalled team development.
Elite young goalie with excellent rate-stat potential and a chance to seize Minnesota’s No. 1 job.
Exceptional long-term scoring talent who could approach a point per game, with a bigger explosion possibly still ahead.
Breakout power forward still only 22; last season’s 73 points likely do not represent his ceiling.
Veteran power-play specialist joining Tampa’s elite offense could have one more major fantasy season.
One of the position’s most reliable goal scorers, though last year’s 60 points were a career high.
Elite real-life defenseman with fantasy upside, but year-to-year injuries and production swings reduce predictability.
Strong multi-category rookie profile creates both a useful floor and significant sophomore upside.
Expected to miss meaningful time with a shoulder injury, but remains capable of strong per-game scoring when back.
Likely regression from a late-age breakout, but Toronto’s power-play role should preserve useful D1/D2 production.
Power-forward upside remains excellent, especially in banger formats, but health and production vary significantly year to year.
Durable, dependable 70-plus-point winger whose upside improves substantially if New Jersey’s stars stay healthy.
Could surge if he remains beside Celebrini; Larkin still prices in some uncertainty rather than projecting the full upside.
Prime-age first-line winger already near a point per game with an ascending center in Fantilli.
Repeated an unusually high shooting percentage, making his breakout more credible despite modest chance-generation metrics.
Still a point-per-game talent, but Florida may manage his workload after major knee injuries.
Useful banger-league winger with goals, points and hits; expect some shooting-percentage regression.
Washington’s stronger roster helps, but its crowded right wing may limit his role and ceiling.
Talented workhorse with strong volume value; Anaheim’s loose defensive play remains the main rate-stat concern.
Normally a reliable 30-goal, 65-point center, but injury and trade turmoil make him a frustrating draft investment.
Bounce-back candidate only a year removed from 40 goals, though recent decline and physical wear create concern.
Returned to a 40-plus-goal pace, but age and recurring injury risk now need to be priced in.
Excellent banger-league target combining 25-plus goals, strong points and heavy hit totals.
Strong Colorado situation and excellent recent results, but Blackwood prevents true workhorse volume.
Still a useful fantasy defenseman, though four consecutive declines in points suggest age-related erosion.
Prime-age power winger capable of roughly 30-40 goals, 70 points and useful banger stats if healthy.
Excellent all-around defenseman and safe low-end D1, though heavy two-way usage may limit elite scoring upside.
New contract signals roughly 50-start 1A usage on a strong Montreal team despite Fowler’s long-term presence.
Past his elite peak but still productive; becomes attractive if drafted cheaply enough to account for injury risk.
Strong assists and points contributor whose low shot volume and inflated shooting percentage limit category value.
Reliable 25-goal, 60-plus-point winger whose established production offers a solid mid-draft floor.
Still provides roughly 30 goals and huge hits, but age and Washington’s added forward depth create downside.
Dependable second fantasy center with heavy minutes and a repeatable mid-60s point floor.
Last season proved he still has scoring left, though an unusually high shooting percentage points toward some regression.
Still capable of 30 goals and 70 points, but age suggests gradual decline rather than another late-career surge.
Even at 41, his power-play deployment and shot remain good enough to support another roughly 30-goal season.
Breakout talent remains, but consistency, unsigned status and a poor start to camp create additional risk.
Career-best production followed his move to Carolina; another roughly 25-goal, 65-point season is reasonable.
Elite per-game producer whose chronic inability to stay healthy makes paying full draft price dangerous.
Larkin’s Calder favorite and potentially Philadelphia’s most dangerous forward, but rookie uncertainty keeps veterans ahead of him.
Heavy workload on an improving Utah team is attractive, though Cossa could reduce his starts somewhat.
Steady secondary goal source who can be counted on for around 30 with a moderate point ceiling.
Similar fantasy profile to Horvat: reliable goals and modest points, helped by Colorado’s stronger environment.
Boom-or-bust bet on Florida’s team context after a poor individual season from the 36-year-old starter.
Back-to-back 35-goal seasons show real scoring ability, but weaker linemates and a huge contract add uncertainty.
Highly talented smaller goalie with major upside; Columbus’ overall trajectory is the biggest concern.
Strong multi-year track record makes last season look like a setback, creating attractive bounce-back value.
Durable enough to offer a useful floor, but fluctuating production and a weaker Rangers roster cap upside.
More shots, a clear No. 1 center role and elite wingers make this a prime breakout opportunity.
Increasingly a floor play because of recurring minor injuries, though his established track record warrants a mulligan.
Highly skilled rookie should receive immediate scoring-line and power-play opportunity on a Toronto team that needs offense.
Now Los Angeles’ primary offensive defenseman and positioned for a major breakout with expanded ice time.
Established 25-goal floor plus potential full-season exposure to Pastrnak creates career-year upside.
Quietly reliable fantasy defenseman with repeated 10-goal, 50-plus-point seasons and strong role security.
Age creates regression risk after a resurgence, but even a meaningful decline could leave him around 50 points.
Still highly productive in Florida, but age, maintenance absences and an early-season injury lower his draft value.
Volatile last season but historically excellent, with weak internal competition making him a reasonable rebound target.
Consistent 30-goal scorer whose shoulder surgery and recurring missed games significantly reduce his immediate value.
Age, declining production and Utah’s crowded forward depth suggest lower minutes and reduced fantasy usefulness.
Useful specialist for goals, shots and hits, but assists and total points remain comparatively weak.
Finally delivered offensively, but physical wear, likely missed games and a six-game suspension argue against chasing the breakout.
Career-high goals came from increased shooting rather than luck; even regression leaves a solid 60-point baseline.
Lower expectations make him a useful value for goals, shots and hits even without major upside.
Consistent 50-plus-point offensive defenseman who lacks star cachet and can therefore be a strong D2 value.
Steady young scorer coming off an excellent playoff run and potentially receiving early first-line opportunity.
Chicago’s huge investment should translate into heavy minutes and power-play usage, creating 60-point breakout potential.
Excellent post-trade scoring pace looks legitimate, though Larkin uses a conservative roughly 60-point projection.
Strong finish revived breakout hopes; still young enough to justify another upside bet.
Career year in Philadelphia appears sustainable enough to treat him as a legitimate scoring-line fantasy forward.
Established himself as a viable starter, but Woll is a stronger workload threat than last season’s backups.
Efficient scorer who can boost goals and power-play points, with prior durability concerns still worth remembering.
Hughes’ arrival has improved Faber’s production enough to offset the lack of first-unit power-play duty.
First-round talent, strong role and post-Olympic surge create an appealing sophomore breakout profile.
Elite natural playmaking remains, but a concerning preseason injury timeline makes him difficult to draft aggressively.
Still a solid D2, but frequent injuries and limited fantasy reward from his broader real-life game reduce upside.
Frequently misses games but remains productive enough to approach 30 goals and 60 points without a full season.
Offense and 200-plus-hit production create strong banger value, though Larkin wants another good season before fully buying in.
Ottawa should give him a major playmaking role beside Stutzle, creating a good chance to exceed his career-best points.
No longer a 100-point player, but 50-60 points plus 100-plus hits still make him shallow-league relevant.
Crowded Washington depth may suppress ceiling, but roughly 20 goals and 60 points remains a very safe expectation.
Poor sophomore season established a usable floor; reduced hype creates profit potential if conditioning and role improve.
Coming off a strong year, but age and limited category contributions make regression more likely than another jump.
High-end talent is held back by second-unit power-play duty behind Heiskanen, limiting his fantasy ceiling.
Excellent real-life agitator whose playoff shot and hit growth hints at a much more valuable fantasy breakout.
Columbus should give him more responsibility, making a roughly 60-point pace plausible despite chronic missed games.
Pro-ready rookie with strong shot volume who could receive major center responsibility while Bedard is injured.
Tuch’s departure opens right-wing opportunity after Doan already established a useful 25-goal floor.
Young No. 2 center coming off a strong Cup run and entering an ideal age for another step forward.
Barkov’s return reduces Bennett’s exceptional workload from last season, though Florida’s depth keeps his floor respectable.
Playing with MacKinnon gives him value, but career production and durability history argue against overpaying.
Age and modest production after returning to Colorado indicate the decline phase is underway.
Useful real-life winger whose lack of power-play deployment sharply limits fantasy ceiling.
Strong power-play goals, shots and hits when active, but his physical style repeatedly costs him games.
Should still produce at a 25-to-30-goal pace, but complications from leg surgery make his return date uncertain.
Blocked from PP1 but remains a strong even-strength producer with a long record of double-digit goals and solid points.
St. Louis paid heavily for him and should give him major responsibility, creating plausible post-hype breakout upside.
Still Seattle’s best fantasy skater and historically durable, though a better playmaking environment would unlock more value.
Starting role on a strong Vegas team offers upside, but inconsistent play and the organization’s short leash create risk.
Reliable mid-draft veteran providing efficient goals, 50-plus points and useful hit totals.
Recent slump may lower his cost even though his multi-year track record still supports 20-plus goals and high-50s points.
Future-star talent with power-play opportunity, but Washington’s crowded wing depth could keep him on Line 3.
Productive with Crosby but highly variable year to year; career averages provide the safest expectation.
Draft for a roughly 50-point floor and hope a trade unlocks his dormant point-per-game talent.
Past his fantasy peak but still a dependable roughly 25-goal option in medium and deeper formats.
Has the early 1A edge, but last season’s back-and-forth with Lyon makes a true workhorse projection unsafe.
Potential starter for the defending champion, but Carolina’s unpredictable goalie deployment and Kochetkov’s upside limit confidence.
Wildly inconsistent career scoring history makes him difficult to project despite occasional excellent seasons.
Above-average in New Jersey with his best workload opportunity in years, though age and team quality cap upside.
Thirty goals came with a major shooting-percentage spike; Larkin expects meaningful scoring regression.
Name value exceeds role certainty as a second-pair, PP2 defenseman in Vegas; fantasy value could disappoint.
Edmonton offers win upside, but age, injury and losing Carolina’s defensive environment create major boom-bust risk.
Played well last year and has succeeded behind weak teams before, though Detroit may suppress wins.
Strong Seattle finish suggests the 29-goal season could repeat, but age and underlying talent keep expectations conservative.
Top-100 talent on a per-game basis, but chronic inability to stay healthy makes a large investment unwise.
Smart, polished prospect capable of immediate NHL impact; ranking reflects willingness to accept being a year early.
Excellent young goalie trapped behind a poor team; worth stashing in case Chicago finally improves.
Secure top-six role and strong post-Olympic production create major breakout upside, with minor injury potentially lowering cost.
Talented young starter whose weak Calgary team will hurt wins and goals-against average.
Useful Colorado 1B with the upside to reclaim the starting job and become a top-15 fantasy goalie.
Trade lowers linemate quality but should increase minutes; late-season scoring pace suggests useful upside remains.
Better real-life than fantasy, but his established goal rate makes 30 possible with a healthy season.
Affordable source of 25-30 goals, though Chicago’s expected plus-minus remains a serious category drag.
Reliable 10-goal, 40-point defenseman and sensible Zero-D target, with contract-year motivation adding mild upside.
Development has been slower than expected, but Bedard’s injury creates an early opportunity for a delayed breakout.
Potential Celebrini linemate after a strong Columbus stint; role uncertainty makes him an intriguing sleeper.
Appears to enter camp as Los Angeles’ starter, but Kuemper should keep the workload close to an even split.
Second-half resurgence showed he still has value, especially for goals and shots from the blue line.
Top rookie-defense scoring candidate, though third-pair and PP2 deployment may initially cap him around the mid-40s.
Still blocked from PP1 by Hamilton; becomes dramatically more valuable if that obstacle disappears.
Late-career risk/reward goalie pick whose value depends on both his own rebound and Toronto’s volatile roster working.
Has outplayed Binnington and earned more starts, but the tandem and St. Louis’ uncertain quality limit excitement.
The 100-point year is long gone, but a roughly 20-goal, 50-point floor remains useful.
Recent elite history is offset by age, last year’s injuries and Carlson competing for power-play time.
Still capable of strong power-play scoring and around 55 points, though Chicago’s plus-minus will hurt.
Remarkably productive for his age, but likely 55-60 games and continued age decline cap total output.
Long-term contract suggests major St. Louis opportunity and a plausible rebound toward his previous 57-point career high.
Leaving Kaprizov and likely missing Los Angeles’ first line lowers his ceiling, though 45 points remains attainable.
Breakout role disappears with Barkov back, returning him to a talented but fantasy-limited third-line position.
Excellent volume goalie for saves and starts, but recent rate stats and Nashville’s quality are concerns.
Outstanding real-life defensive center whose third-line role caps fantasy upside around last year’s mid-40s points.
No longer his old self, but improved late-season and playoff form makes him draftable in medium and deeper leagues.
Still capable of a 60-plus-point level, but health and Washington’s deep center group create role risk.
Strong underlying player entering a crowded Utah depth chart; needs top-six placement to retain fantasy relevance.
Must-draft banger asset thanks to a stable 20-goal floor and enormous hit totals.
Assist-heavy profile gains upside after moving to New Jersey, particularly if he receives time with Jack Hughes.
Steady 20-goal, 50-point two-way center with little expectation of a meaningful offensive ceiling beyond that.
Under-the-radar rookie with strong chance-generation skill who dominated the AHL and may offer late-draft value.
Calgary’s thin depth guarantees opportunity, supporting another roughly 20-goal, 200-shot season.
Vancouver caps his ceiling, but 20-plus goals and around 50 points remain reasonable; plus-minus is a major concern.
Still capable of roughly 25 goals after a Boston rebound, but recurring injury risk remains substantial.
Early NHL results lean playmaker, while his junior scoring history suggests significant untapped goal upside.
Bussi starts ahead, but Kochetkov’s age and upside give him a realistic path to flipping the Carolina tandem.
Expect 20-plus goals with limited ceiling in Vancouver; a trade would be the clearest path to more value.
Heavy post-Hughes minutes make him a useful Zero-D target, though Vancouver’s plus-minus environment is dangerous.
Montreal’s deeper lineup likely reduces his role versus Anaheim, modestly lowering his fantasy outlook.
Unexciting but reliable veteran who should supply 20-plus goals and around 50 points in St. Louis’ top six.
Career-best season showed talent, but modest 15-minute usage makes a repeat more likely than another leap.
Lower ceiling than Parekh but much safer redraft role because Calgary is paying him for heavy minutes.
Opportunity exists for more even-strength and PP2 work, giving him a realistic path toward roughly 40 points.
KHL goal-scoring leader appears NHL-ready and can be taken very late before casual drafters recognize him.
Pittsburgh’s offseason choices signal confidence; could begin as 1B and overtake Silovs for the lead job.
Strong NHL finish, elite prospect pedigree and possible first-line role make him an appealing overlooked breakout candidate.
Year-2 leap-of-faith pick whose raw offensive talent and strong camp buzz justify chasing the upside.
Already supplies goals, shots and hits; increased ice time creates breakout potential despite Seattle’s weak environment.
Thirty goals are unlikely to repeat at last year’s shooting efficiency, with health and top-six role also uncertain.
High-upside puck-moving, physical defenseman whose current unsigned, absent status makes him impossible to value aggressively.
Still carries enormous long-term goalie upside, but current NHL performance has not justified an aggressive redraft price.
Dependable source of roughly 20 goals and 200 hits, though Utah’s improving depth may gradually reduce his role.
Useful across categories when active, but recurring physical problems make missed games a persistent concern.
Improved supporting cast helped his production, but hip surgery makes him a late-round stash rather than immediate contributor.
Underlying save percentage remains strong, but Seattle’s poor roster sharply limits his win and overall fantasy ceiling.
Heavy minutes and PP1 role keep him relevant in deep leagues despite limited belief in his offensive upside or team.
Elite goalie prospect who should play enough to matter, though a serious challenge for Dobes is more likely next season.
Strong per-game banger producer with severe durability issues and a reduced Washington role that may hurt even when healthy.
Dominated junior and the AHL and flashed in the NHL; enormous upside depends almost entirely on where Washington deploys him.
Could be a major bargain if he stays beside Celebrini after quietly producing well in a small rookie sample.
Safe 45-to-50-point veteran who is more useful as a streamer than a late draft pick when higher-upside options exist.
Young top-six winger already broke out modestly and now enters his prime in an improving San Jose offense.
Low-upside assist-oriented center; Larkin strongly prefers using this draft range on boom-or-bust players instead.
Immediate No. 2 center role in Vancouver creates a path to 50-plus points and possibly the top job.
Versatile real-life center whose fantasy contribution is mostly points and could shrink if Helenius passes him.
Late-career depth option who can still supply assists and power-play points but will hover around the roster bubble.
Hip surgery and Wallstedt’s rise cost him the 1A job, though he remains useful whenever healthy enough to start.
Last season’s unexpected offense is difficult to trust because he had never scored at that level previously.
Still elite for hits and blocks, with some rebound scoring potential in a prominent role on improving Utah.
Strong late banger target providing shots, hits, roughly 20 goals and around 40 points.
Elite prospect should receive every opportunity to inherit a major Vancouver role; breakout timing is uncertain but ceiling is special.
Excellent dynasty asset, but Vejmelka’s workhorse role and Cossa’s minimal NHL experience call for redraft patience.
Strong real-life defenseman whose lack of power-play opportunity caps fantasy ceiling; PP1 deployment would radically change his value.
Surprising offense added to an already physical profile, and age 24 leaves room for another step.
Back issues and limited upside make him unexciting, though a second-line center role keeps him draftable in deep formats.
Productive on a per-game basis but reliably misses significant time, so managers need injury-list depth behind him.
Useful goals-and-hits winger who appears to have plateaued because St. Louis’ top-six wing spots are crowded.
Edmonton’s shallow wing depth and his strong AHL season create another opportunity for a meaningful scoring-line role.
Seventeen rookie goals plus a newly opened top-six role make a larger sophomore breakout plausible.
Massive long-term upside, but youth, Calgary’s weak roster and competition from Nemec make this a cautious redraft year.
Efficient power-play scorer could find a useful Pittsburgh role and has sleeper potential for roughly 25 goals.
Minnesota still values his center upside; sticking with Kaprizov could allow him to roughly double his rookie point total.
Last year’s 58 points look like a late-career outlier, with Monahan competition making him an easy fade.
Proven scorer at every level whose limited NHL minutes have hidden intriguing goal upside.
Clearly behind Vladar initially, but No. 1-caliber talent makes him a high-end backup capable of forcing a larger share.
Solid player whose long-awaited breakout never materialized; Larkin no longer expects a major offensive leap.
Former KHL scorer may get a Kaprizov audition, making him an interesting deep-league sleeper despite a quiet rookie year.
Little ceiling remains, but Anaheim top-six minutes still make him useful for assists in deeper formats.
Heavy minutes should generate shots, hits and blocks, though last season’s scoring is not reliable enough to project again.
Potential Colorado top-six opportunity creates a late-career sleeper case, but third-line usage is equally plausible.
Can still score, but shrinking ice time and San Jose’s crowded depth make reaching 20 goals more difficult.
Endgame goalie stash with league-winning upside if aging Markstrom falters behind Florida’s strong team.
Talented puck mover finally settled in Philadelphia, but fantasy scoring has yet to exceed a modest 32-point ceiling.
Reasonable Zero-D depth defenseman who can contribute goals and shots despite Seattle’s uninspiring environment.
Do not chase last year’s 55 points; younger San Jose forwards should push the career depth center down the lineup.
Useful assists and plus-minus come incidentally from playing with Edmonton’s stars, but limited PP work caps upside.
Only a year removed from major fantasy value; camp battle with Forsberg will determine which Kings goalie is worth rostering.
Heavy minutes create deep-league volume value, roughly mid-30s points and useful blocks despite limited offensive upside.
Minnesota may reduce his minutes, but a floor around 20 goals and 150 hits keeps him playable in banger formats.
Specialist banger pick whose extraordinary 413-hit season gives him elite value in that single category.
May open as Pittsburgh’s starter, but Larkin expects Murashov to eventually take the job.
Reliable deep-league defenseman for 30-plus points and heavy blocks with little upside beyond the floor.
Returning from ACL surgery and highly injury prone, but Dallas’ thinner depth could create useful opportunity when healthy.
Established Colorado top-four defenseman with 40-point potential, though last season benefited significantly from Makar’s injury absence.
Typically around 20 goals and 40 points, with inconsistent line placement limiting reliability and upside.
Twenty-two rookie goals show shooting talent, but a role that can range from Line 2 to Line 4 adds uncertainty.
Capable of excellent stretches but likely limited to roughly 30-35 starts behind Luukkonen; best used as a streamer.
Recent top-eight pick has a genuine path to Winnipeg’s No. 2 center job and could become one of the season’s better rookies.
Potential San Jose PP1 quarterback with major late-round breakout upside if camp deployment confirms the role.
Veteran should still score around 40 points, but late drafts are better used on upside before falling back to Hall-type waiver options.
Coming off 21 goals with a plausible Matthews-line audition; training-camp deployment will determine his sleeper value.
Young offensive defenseman is blocked by Werenski but becomes very interesting if injury or trade opens the top role.
Projected Edmonton second-liner offers high-teens goals and 200-plus hits, with some lingering upside from his prospect pedigree.
Starts lower in Boston’s lineup but has enough investment and prior Pastrnak exposure to carry meaningful top-six upside.
Will outscore some players ranked higher, but PP2 status and limited category breadth leave almost no breakout ceiling.
Useful real-life third-line center whose 47-point season may be difficult to repeat in the same role.
Surprisingly healthy last year and only one season removed from strong scoring; useful if he wins Columbus’ No. 2 center job.
Early-season role is uncertain, but substantial prospect upside remains and Boston’s top-six competition is beatable.
Rough NHL start, but a broad Seider-like fantasy toolkit makes him a worthwhile last-pick upside gamble.
High-end goal-scoring prospect who could immediately become a notable rookie scorer if he makes Utah out of camp.
Solid rookie year and AHL playoff experience help, but fantasy relevance depends heavily on earning more than bottom-six deployment.
Low-upside veteran, but Los Angeles’ weak center depth could put him between quality scoring wingers.
Scoring-line vacancy in Dallas gives the physical sophomore a real opportunity after a useful 30-point rookie season.
Playoff goal explosion was driven by unsustainable shooting, though second-line chemistry gives him a little late-round intrigue.
Dominant AHL scorer has a real opening while Jarvis is injured and could make himself difficult to remove from Carolina’s lineup.
Growing minutes and physical category value make him draftable, but unsigned status creates immediate uncertainty.
Reliable 20-goal veteran and waiver option, though sports-hernia recovery will delay the start of his season.
Still capable of another 20-goal season in the right environment, but remaining unsigned this late makes his NHL role highly uncertain.

writeup_note: writeup_summary contains a concise paraphrase of Matt Larkin's analysis from the Daily Faceoff article; it is not the article's verbatim text.
